fields.sections.6.h: Diverse Inspiration Sources and Technical Hybridity
fields.sections.0.ko: This site is a creative platform that provides tutorials enabling users to fold and fly a variety of designs themselves alongside paper airplane product sales. It is designed to serve both hobby enthusiasts and beginners by presenting both product purchase and DIY creation options.
fields.sections.1.ko: Multiple designs featured on the platform cite objective performance metrics. For example, Unite holds the world record with a flight time of 31.2 seconds, and the Arrowhead tutorial is stated to have received over 100 million views. These figures serve as evidence validating the reliability and popularity of each design.
fields.sections.2.ko: The featured aircraft are segmented by flight method and application. They include gliders pursuing pure gliding performance (Liberty Airsled, Palladium), designs tracing rotational or boomerang trajectories (Spinner, Looper), and projectile-type designs targeting maximum distance flight (Plasma X, Quill), configured to allow users to select based on desired flight characteristics.
fields.sections.3.ko: Numerous aircraft names are followed by designer attribution in the format "Designed by [name]" or "by [name]". This grants ownership recognition to individual creators and reinforces the community structure by recruiting and validating new designs through contests such as the 2025 Paper Airplane Championship winners featured on the site (Orion, Fork-Wing).
fields.sections.4.ko: The featured designs span a wide range from a difficulty perspective. The spectrum ranges from explicit beginner-level simple folding (Vapor, Atlas) to advanced origami techniques described as "very difficult" (Durandal, Eclipse). This stratification appears intended to lower entry barriers while satisfying experienced practitioners' desire for deeper learning.
fields.sections.5.ko: Multiple aircraft descriptions frequently repeat distance units such as "over 100 feet flight", "capable of 150 feet flight", and "80 feet flight". This structure enables quantitative comparison of each design's competitiveness, guiding user selection on a data-driven basis. However, it remains unclear whether these figures have undergone official verification.
fields.sections.6.ko: The designs reference multilayered cultural and technical sources including real aircraft (SU-27, SU-57, F-102, X-15 and other Russian and American fighter jet motifs), classic dart folds, and Japanese paper-folding techniques (see Nakamura Lock). Explicit attribution such as "Nakamura Lock, by Eiji Nakamura" demonstrates creativity through inheriting existing origami tradition while adding novel modifications and optimizations.
fields.sections.7.ko: The overall composition implies a premium-basic model that recruits users through free or low-cost tutorial content and then monetizes through completed kit or related product sales. While official management information is absent, the structure combines high viewership (Arrowhead 100 million views) with community activation strategies such as contest hosting, suggesting an orientation toward building brand loyalty within the hobby market.
fields.caveat: The source material consists only of product listings and basic feature descriptions; verified data on business scale, investment status, and user statistics are entirely absent, making analysis limited to the structure of the platform as a community entity.
